A 89-year-old woman with stage IV breast adenocarcinoma metastatic to the liver and lungs is
incidentally found to have a new moderate right-sided pleural effusion on a routine chest CT. She is
asymptomatic, with normal vital signs and an oxygen saturation of 95% on ambient air. Pleural-fluid
analysis from a diagnostic thoracentesis reveals the following: | | Patient value | | --- | --- | | pH | 7.30 | |
Total protein (g/dL) | 3.1 | | Lactate dehydrogenase (U/liter) | 247 | Concurrent serum values are as
follows: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | | Total protein (g/dL) | 5.8 | 5.5–8.0 | | Lactate
dehydrogenase (U/liter) | 180 | 100–190 | Gram stain is negative, and cytology demonstrates scattered,
rounded clusters of cells with irregular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. What is the most appropriate
management approach for this patient’s pleural effusion? Answer Choices: (A) Video-assisted
thoracoscopic surgery (B) Initiation of targeted therapy (C) Antibiotic therapy (D) Observation (E) Chest
tube placement (F) Repeated therapeutic thoracenteses (G) Chemical pleurodesis (H) Placement of a
pleural catheter (I) Systemic corticosteroids (J) Pleural biopsy
 A. Placement of a pleural catheter
B. Repeated therapeutic thoracenteses
C. Systemic corticosteroids
